rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for drops splashing or spattering, without stressing a deliberate cause or a particular target.

example.english: The water can splatter everywhere when I wash the car.
example.traditional: 洗車嗰陣啲水濺到成身都係。
example.jyutping: sai2 ce1 go2 zan6 di1 seoi2 zin3 dou3 seng4 san1 dou1 hai6

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose noun for marks or mess left by splashing, especially paint or oil on a surface.

example.english: There are some oil splatter marks on the table that won't come off.
example.traditional: 張枱有啲油污漬，抹極都仲喺度。
example.jyutping: zoeng1 ci4 jau5 di1 jau4 wu1 zik1 mut3 gik6 dou1 zung6 hai2 dou6

rows.jyutping: N cin2 dou3 zau1 wai4 dou1 hai6
rows.note: Use this pattern when the key idea is that the substance has splashed over the surrounding area.

example.english: The oil splatter got all over the place and made the whole kitchen dirty.
example.traditional: 啲油濺到周圍都係，搞到成個廚房都污糟晒。
example.jyutping: di1 jau4 zin3 dou3 zau1 wai4 dou1 hai6 gaau2 dou3 seng4 go3 cyu4 fong2 dou1 wu1 zou1 saai3

rows.traditional: 將 A 濺到 B 上
rows.jyutping: zoeng1 A cin2 dou3 B soeng6
rows.note: Use this when saying that someone causes a liquid or other splattable substance to land messily on a surface.

example.english: I accidentally splatter water onto the table.
example.traditional: 我唔小心將杯水濺到張枱上。
example.jyutping: ngo5 m4 siu2 sam1 zoeng1 bui1 seoi2 zin3 dou3 zoeng1 ci4 soeng6

rows.note: Use this for the gory horror-film genre rather than for a physical splash or stain.

example.english: I don't watch splatter horror films because they scare me too much.
example.traditional: 我唔睇血腥恐怖片，驚到瞓唔着。
example.jyutping: ngo5 m4 tai2 hyut3 seng1 hung2 bou3 pin2 geng1 dou3 fan3 m4 zoek6

rows.note: Use this when the drops specifically spatter a person or land all over them.

example.english: The car may splatter muddy water all over me.
example.traditional: 架車駛過水氹，啲泥水濺到我身上。
example.jyutping: gaa3 ce1 sai2 gwo3 seoi2 tam5 di1 nai4 seoi2 zin3 dou3 ngo5 san1 soeng6
